subject: Eight schools will student level data- vectorization?

messages.author: b644a619d5622105
messages.subject: Eight schools will student level data- vectorization?
parts:
I'm interested in vectorizing a model that looks similar to the eight schools example, except where you might have student-level data. So imagine the data consisted of a student score and their school. I can get a for loop to work like this:

data {
  int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
  int,lower=0> n; //number of students
  real score[n]; // test score for each student
  int school[n]; //school for each student
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
  for (index in 1:n) {
    score[index] ~ normal(mu[school[index]], sigma);
  }
}

But I can't seem to vectorize the model. Taking out "[index]" on both sides doesn't work because score and mu[school] are not vectors of the same dimension.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Eight schools will student level data- vectorization?
parts:
Correct --- we don't have composition of indexing the way
you might expect from R. The only way to vectorize

> y[index] ~ normal(mu[school[index]], sigma);

is:

{
vector[n] mu_school;
for (i in 1:n)
mu_school[i] <- mu[school[i]];
y ~ normal(mu_school, sigma);
}

That should be faster, but it's ugly.

- Bob
